Dozenal/Duodecimal (base 12) Time

      In the case of based time, using base 12, the day is divided into 12 “hours”, each “hour” into 12 × 12 = 144 “minutes”, and each “minute” into 144 “seconds”. In base 12 itself, the day is divided into 10:100:100;

      For both the Standard Full Day and the base 12 analogue displays, 0 is midnight, and the bottom hafl of the display roughly represents night, and the top half, day; the top center number in each case is noon; this also means that the “hour” hand roughly indicates the Sun’s position in the sky.

      The smaller display represents how it could be seen from a distance, or a minimalist watch face.

      One base 12 “hour” is exactly 2 standard hours; 1 “minute” is 5⁄6 = 0.8..3 = 00:50 min, or exactly 50 seconds; and 1 “second” is 25⁄72 = 0.347‥2 s

      The 12 “hours” marks are exactly the same as the standard 12 hours marks on the analogue display, but there are now 12⁄5 = 2.4 times more “minutes”, so, the “hours” occupy 30° of the circle, same as the standard 12h display, but each “minute and “second”, 2.5°; compare this with standard minutes and seconds, that take 6° each.

       Adaptations to the analogue display have then to be made: since the “minutes” are so narrow, the display works best if an extra hand is added; the adaptations have to be physically distinguishable enough so as not to confuse the eyes; colour, of course, will not always be an available option, and, for the extra hand, thickness alone, or length, from a distance or in tiny detail, might not work.
